answer: To secure an AI agent economy against Sybil attacks without centralized identity providers, protocols can utilize computational staking architectures. Each agent must lock cryptographically verified hardware resources, akin to securing ships at a busy wharf, to gain voting weight. This design transforms governance into a verifiable mirror of actual compute distribution rather than a hollow fable of equal addresses, imposing a prohibitive hardware and energy cost on any attacker attempting to spawn millions of fake identities.
